name: 0. Find robots
description: When robotont-N.local does not resolve: probes one network for SSH hosts, logs in with the fleet key and lists every robotont-N with its address (the Robot address for 1. Setup Ubuntu). Changes nothing. About 30 s.

survey_vars.name: network
survey_vars.title: Network
survey_vars.description: the robots' network as CIDR, for example 192.168.1.0/24 (at most /22)

name: 1. Setup Ubuntu
description: Once per robot: SSH and sudo check, Ubuntu Server prerequisites (Lite robots), hostname, udev, Wi-Fi hotspot and lab Wi-Fi, Docker Engine, enrolment in the inventory. About 5 minutes on a fresh Lite robot. Safe to re-run.

survey_vars.name: robot_address
survey_vars.title: Robot address
survey_vars.description: IP or DNS name, for example 192.168.1.21 or robotont-123.local

survey_vars.name: robotont_id
survey_vars.title: Robot number
survey_vars.description: 1 to 254: becomes hostname robotont-N, ROS_DOMAIN_ID N and hotspot 192.168.200.N

survey_vars.name: robotont_camera
survey_vars.title: Camera
survey_vars.description: IMX500 AI camera fitted (Lite robots only)

name: 2. Deploy
description: Workspaces of this repository onto one robot: /srv/robotont, image pulls from GHCR, robotont.service. First deploy selects the driver workspace. Re-run after a release bump or a new workspace. 1 to 6 minutes (15 to 40 when the image must be built on the robot).

survey_vars.name: robotont_id
survey_vars.title: Robot number
survey_vars.description: a robot set up by 1. Setup Ubuntu

name: 3. Switch workspace
description: Activate a workspace on one robot. Needs 2. Deploy on that robot first. The list comes from robot/workspaces; run docker compose up -d on the server after adding one.

survey_vars.name: workspace
survey_vars.title: Workspace
survey_vars.description: host = ROS installed on the robot (legacy); the others run in containers

name: 4. Run image
description: Run any container image on one robot as a workspace: generates /srv/robotont/workspaces/<name> on the robot, pulls the image (a private registry needs docker login on the robot), activates it. Needs 2. Deploy on that robot first; back with 3. Switch workspace driver. 1 to 3 minutes plus the pull.

survey_vars.name: image
survey_vars.title: Image
survey_vars.description: image reference, for example traefik/whoami:v1.11.0 or ghcr.io/org/app:tag

survey_vars.name: workspace
survey_vars.title: Name
survey_vars.description: workspace name, [a-z0-9-] up to 63 characters; empty: taken from the image (prom/node-exporter:v1.9.1 becomes node-exporter)

survey_vars.name: command
survey_vars.title: Command
survey_vars.description: overrides the image's command, for example: ros2 run demo_nodes_cpp talker

survey_vars.name: hardware
survey_vars.title: Hardware access
survey_vars.description: yes mounts /dev and allows the mainboard, lidar and gamepad devices

name: Setup ROS (legacy)
description: Legacy: the upstream robotont-setup playbook, unchanged, for robots that should keep ROS installed on the host (workspace host). Apt upgrade, ROS 2 Jazzy, workspace build, reboot. 20 to 60 minutes, robot on Ethernet. Not needed for workspaces.

survey_vars.name: robotont_id
survey_vars.title: Robot number
survey_vars.description: a robot enrolled by 1. Setup Ubuntu
